parsed.explanation: The combined regime is split: national entry and custody rules are actively hostile and traveller-facing, while this state/province layer is protective and demonstrably enforced. National passport/visa practice requires markers to match birth sex, instructs officers to refuse cases with discrepancies and to consider lifetime misrepresentation findings; reports document passports blocked or confiscated and travellers stranded. Immigration custody shows documented abuse of trans detainees. Against that, the state/province's public-accommodations, housing and employment protections cover gender identity, hate-crime enhancements are in force, the panic defence is abolished, and a July 2026 court applied the civil-rights statute for an assault on a trans woman. Everyday visitor life is comparatively protected; the exposure concentrates at the border and in any downstream detention.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy accepts only M/F markers matching birth sex; officers instructed to refuse discrepant cases and consider material-misrepresentation findings; passports reportedly blocked or confiscated, some travellers stranded; athlete-entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; misrepresentation finding is not automatic and requires four elements with limited waivers; litigation ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport marker mismatch triggers national secondary screening regardless of state-level protections; state law cannot override border adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for visitors in immigration custody; a prison-related executive order was rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can escalate into immigration detention, moving the traveller from a protective state into a hostile national custody system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans exist in a minority of states, four with criminal trespass triggers; a 2025 arrest of a trans student in a capitol restroom, held in a men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province's public-accommodations law covers gender identity and expression; no local facility ban documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National buildings and other states' facilities carry exposure; locally, accommodation access is legally protected.

care_services.exposure: National measures pressure gender-affirming care; this state/province banned minors' care in 2024-2025 with provider discipline and rights to sue.
care_services.protection: Adult care not restricted locally; anti-discrimination coverage extended to health care since 2020; conversion-therapy ban in force.
care_services.interaction: Visitor adults are largely unaffected; a travelling family with a trans minor faces a hostile national framing, though no visitor-facing care rule is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for prioritised neutralisation; justice-department reward guidance invokes 'radical gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; courts have enjoined several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Frames advocacy and visible trans presence as security-relevant, raising scrutiny risk at national checkpoints; local police and courts operate under protective state law.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders characterise minors' transition care as mutilation and direct investigation of schools facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for visiting minors; state anti-bullying and school protections cover gender identity.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a visibly trans minor faces elevated border questioning risk; no documented detention of visiting minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents recorded in 2025, second-highest raw count, but no per-capita denominator; local sources describe the state as least safe in the region, an attributed characterisation.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate-crime enhancements since 2019; panic defence abolished 2024; documented 2026 civil-rights judgment for assault on a trans woman; 88% public support for protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists locally and has been used; raw counts carry no rate, so violence is not shown to exceed background.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport-marker litigation and challenges to the executive orders are unresolved; exposure depends on which measures are in force at travel.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, a legal-aid FAQ, and functioning state civil-rights enforcement.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies cannot reach border adjudication or national custody; state recourse covers accommodation, services and violence only.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar denial-of-entry mechanics with invasive review and no detention, but that anchor has no documented custody abuse and no local protection statute; here entry refusal can chain into abusive national detention, partly offset by enforced state anti-discrimination law. Roughly comparable, marginally higher.

That anchor's discrepancy is resolved by a supervisor applying transit guidelines, with a functioning remedy. Here national entry rules deliberately refuse discrepant cases and remedies sit in unresolved litigation, so this jurisdiction sits materially lower.

That anchor involves extortion, coerced statements and threatened imprisonment under public-order statutes. Here no criminal penalty attaches to trans status itself and state law protects services and violence recourse, so this jurisdiction sits clearly higher.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences two regimes at once. At the border, national document rules require markers congruent with birth sex, authorise refusal and possible lifetime misrepresentation findings, and have produced blocked or confiscated passports and stranded travellers; downstream immigration custody carries documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse. Inside this state/province, by contrast, public-accommodations and hate-crime law cover gender identity, the panic defence is abolished, and enforcement is documented in a 2026 judgment. The rating reflects a hostile, universal national exposure at the crossing and in custody, discounted but not cancelled by a genuinely protective local sphere. Minors' care bans and incident counts are resident-facing or denominator-free and carry little weight.
